newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil foreign investments to hit record in '96.
newsitem.headline: Brazil foreign investments to hit record in '96.

text.p: A study of multinational companies says foreign investment in Brazil will hit record levels in 1996 at $9 billion, a newspaper said.

The study by the Brazilian Society for the Study of Transnational Companies (Sobeet) estimates that $7.5 billion in foreign investment will enter Brazil by December, a figure which could reach $9 billion if investments by foreign companies located in Brazil are included, O Globo said.
In 1997, Sobeet forecasts foreign investment to reach $10 billion.
The study says more foreign companies operate in Brazil than in any other developing country with 382 of the 500 top multinationals listed by Forbes magazine present in Brazil, O Globo said.
Companies from the United States alone invested $1.179 billion in Brazil between January and August, O Globo said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
